brief: BofA's Hartnett, risk-off for six straight Flow Shows, frames 2027 around two questions: when do hikes end, and do they end before recession. His trigger for an early stop is S&P below 6,845 (erasing 2026's gains) plus IG CDX above 80bps; Friday's 6,925 close leaves the index 80 points away. If the Fed instead treats post-midterm inflation as its priority, the earliest hikes end is the March 18 or April 28 FOMC, and hard-landing risk rises until then. Fed officials (Cook, Paulson, the minutes) still sound hawkish. Hartnett argues pricing has capitulated but positioning hasn't (3.6% cash, 3% expecting hard landing, $310bn into equity funds), so he wants positioning capitulation before an all-clear. His hard-landing case: consensus GDP and EPS forecasts rest on fading household wealth and AI capex, whose financing strain (hyperscaler free cash flow going to -$283bn in 2027) is forcing a slowdown; confirmation would be jobless claims above 250K and IG spreads above 100bps, triggering a rotation out of stocks into bonds, China, the dollar and anti-AI assets. He weighs both the 2018 (quick Fed pivot) and 2000 (early pivot, bear market continues on earnings) analogs, leaning toward the latter.
